enhanced.fullText:
The Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) is a comprehensive web-based database mandated by the USA PATRIOT Act and codified under 8 U.S.C. § 1372, designed to track and monitor international students and exchange visitors in the United States. Administered by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) through the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP), SEVIS serves as the primary mechanism for government oversight of F-1, M-1, and J-1 visa holders at certified educational institutions.

Under 8 CFR § 214.3 and 8 CFR § 214.4, higher education institutions certified by SEVP must maintain accurate, real-time records for all F-1 academic students and M-1 vocational students. The regulation requires designated school officials (DSOs) to report significant events within 21 days, including enrollment changes, address modifications, disciplinary actions, and academic program alterations. Institutions must verify student enrollment within 30 days of the program start date and conduct periodic reviews of student status.

SEVIS compliance extends beyond basic record-keeping to encompass comprehensive student lifecycle management. Universities must issue Form I-20 documents through SEVIS, maintain current residential addresses, monitor academic progress, and report any violations of student status. Under 8 CFR § 214.3(k), institutions must report students who fail to maintain status, including those who drop below full-time enrollment, engage in unauthorized employment, or violate program requirements.

Enforcement mechanisms include institutional penalties ranging from compliance warnings to certification withdrawal. ICE conducts regular site visits and compliance reviews, with non-compliance potentially resulting in loss of authorization to enroll international students under 8 CFR § 214.3(j). Recent updates include enhanced cybersecurity protocols and streamlined reporting procedures implemented in 2023.

The regulation imposes specific obligations on institutional officials, including mandatory training for DSOs and backup DSOs. Universities must maintain SEVIS access security, ensure data accuracy, and establish internal compliance protocols. Financial penalties for non-compliance can reach $10,000 per violation, while systematic failures may result in permanent program suspension, affecting institutional ability to serve international student populations critical to higher education diversity and revenue.
enhanced.summary: SEVIS requires higher education institutions to maintain real-time records of F-1 and M-1 international students through a federal database system. Universities must report enrollment changes, address updates, and status violations within prescribed timeframes while ensuring continuous compliance monitoring.
enhanced.requirements:
## Student Record Management
- Maintain accurate SEVIS records for all F-1/M-1 students within 21 days of enrollment changes
- Verify student enrollment within 30 days of program start date
- Update student addresses and contact information within 21 days of notification
- Issue and manage Form I-20 documents exclusively through SEVIS portal

## Status Monitoring and Reporting
- Report academic standing changes including drops below full-time enrollment
- Document disciplinary actions affecting student immigration status
- Monitor and report unauthorized employment violations
- Conduct periodic academic progress reviews per program requirements

## Personnel and Security Requirements
- Designate certified DSOs and backup DSOs with current SEVP training
- Maintain secure access protocols and password management systems
- Establish internal compliance review procedures and documentation standards
- Implement cybersecurity measures protecting student immigration data

## Institutional Compliance
- Submit to periodic ICE site visits and compliance audits
- Maintain certification through continuous regulatory adherence
- Establish appeals procedures for student status determinations
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Report enrollment changes, address updates, and status violations within 21 days via SEVIS portal. Verify new student enrollment within 30 days of program start. Submit annual compliance certifications to SEVP. Report immediately any cybersecurity breaches or unauthorized data access incidents.
